title: Hip replacement
description: A hip replacement is an outpatient surgical procedure where your surgeon removes damaged bone and cartilage from your hip joint and replaces it with artificial components made of metal, plastic, or ceramic. Hip replacement is performed when arthritis or other damage makes your hip painful and stiff. The surgery takes about 1-2 hours, and you may go home the same day or stay overnight. After surgery, you'll use crutches or a walker and begin physical therapy immediately. You can put weight on your new hip right away in most cases. Full recovery typically takes 3-6 months. You'll need to follow activity restrictions for several weeks to protect your new hip. Most patients experience significant pain relief and improved mobility after hip replacement. Your surgeon may perform several variations of this procedure depending on your specific hip damage. This type of procedure can be performed various ways, including acetabuloplasty and partial replacement or revision and total, and the cost may vary depending on the extent of the procedure.
